assumptions.assumption: 'Large track files' means Bytes strictly greater than 10,323,804; the cutoff value itself is excluded.

Bytes is cast to REAL before dividing, so integer division does not truncate the ratio. Tracks with NULL Bytes are dropped by the filter, and Milliseconds is NOT NULL, so no further NULL handling is needed. The track count per media type is the count of tracks passing the size filter.

alternatives.interpretation: The cutoff is inclusive: tracks with Bytes greater than or equal to 10,323,804 count as large.

assumptions.assumption: 'Large' means Bytes strictly greater than 10,323,804 (the cutoff itself is excluded).
Bytes is cast to REAL before dividing so integer division doesn't truncate the bytes-per-millisecond ratio.

The track count per media type is the number of large tracks in that group. Tracks with NULL Bytes are already excluded by the size filter, and Milliseconds is NOT NULL, so this equals the count of tracks with a usable ratio.

alternatives.interpretation: 'Large' is inclusive: Bytes at or above 10,323,804.

assumptions.assumption: 'Large' tracks are those with Bytes strictly greater than 10,323,804 (tracks with NULL Bytes are excluded by the filter).

Track count per media type is the number of large tracks in that group; the average bytes-per-millisecond is computed per track as Bytes/Milliseconds, then averaged within each media type, then averaged across media types (unweighted).

alternatives.interpretation: The cutoff is inclusive: large tracks are those with Bytes >= 10,323,804.
